sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Decline Barbell Bench Press is a compound chest exercise performed on a bench set to a decline angle (typically 15-30 degrees).

This movement emphasizes the lower portion of the pectoralis major, while also engaging the triceps and anterior deltoids.

The decline angle reduces shoulder strain and can allow for heavier loading compared to flat or incline presses.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Emphasizes the lower chest for balanced development
- Allows for heavier weights due to reduced shoulder involvement
- Reduces stress on the shoulders compared to flat/incline presses
- Builds pressing strength and triceps
- Useful for breaking through chest training plateaus
- Can improve lockout strength for other pressing movements

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Pectoralis Major (Sternal Head / Lower Chest)

Secondary: Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids, Serratus Anterior, Core Stabilizers

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Lie flat on a decline bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
2. Grip the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing forward.
3. Keep your elbows bent and unrack the barbell, holding it above your lower chest.
4. Retract your shoulder blades and keep them pressed into the bench.
5. Maintain a slight natural arch in your lower back.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Push the barbell upward until your arms are fully extended, keeping your shoulder blades down and back.
2. Lower the barbell in a controlled manner to your lower chest.
3. Keep your elbows at a 45-60 degree angle from your torso.
4. Touch the bar lightly to your chest—no bouncing.
5. Press the barbell back up to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Letting hips rise off the bench
- Bouncing the bar off the chest
- Flaring elbows out to 90 degrees
- Not retracting shoulder blades
- Using too steep a decline angle
- Rushing the descent
- Not controlling the bar path
- Not using a spotter for heavy sets

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Olympic Barbell (45 lbs/20 kg)
- Weight Plates
- Decline Bench with Rack
- Safety Pins or Spotter Arms (recommended)
- Optional: Spotter for heavy lifts
- Optional: Wrist Wraps
- Optional: Chalk
- Recommended: Flat-soled shoes

sections.heading: Bench and Rack Setup
sections.content:
1. Set the bench to a 15-30 degree decline.
2. Position the bench so the bar racks at a comfortable height.
3. Set safety pins just below chest level.
4. Ensure the bench is stable and centered under the bar.
5. Secure your feet under the foot pads.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Eyes: Directly under or slightly in front of the barbell.
2. Feet: Secured under foot pads.
3. Hips: Firmly on the bench at all times.
4. Back: Pressed into the decline pad, shoulder blades retracted.
5. Shoulders: Pulled back and down into the bench.
6. Head: Resting against the bench pad, neutral position.
7. Grip: Slightly wider than shoulder-width, full grip with thumbs wrapped.
8. Wrists: Stacked straight over forearms.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Flat Barbell Bench Press: Overall chest emphasis
- Decline Dumbbell Press: Greater range of motion, independent arms
- Low-to-High Cable Fly: Constant tension on lower chest
- Machine Decline Press: Guided movement, beginner-friendly
- Decline Push-Ups: Bodyweight lower chest option

sections.heading: Decline Press Variations
sections.content:
Standard Decline Barbell Press: Classic lower chest builder
Close-Grip Decline Press: Triceps emphasis
Wide-Grip Decline Press: Greater chest stretch
Paused Decline Press: Pause on chest for strength off the bottom
Tempo Decline Press: Controlled eccentric
Decline Board Press: Partial range for lockout strength

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Use a shallower decline or switch to dumbbells
Wrist Pain: Use wrist wraps, check grip width
Lower Back Pain: Reduce arch, ensure hips stay on the bench
No Decline Bench: Use a flat bench with plates under one end
No Spotter: Use a power rack with safety pins or switch to dumbbells
No Barbell: Use dumbbells, resistance bands, or machine decline press
Learning Stage: Start with just the bar, focus on bar path and control
